thread:
olivia: FYI customer Acme hit weird embeddings mismatch + billing spike. They sent gzipped NDJSON and we returned a single embedding (vectors=1) but they expected 3. Logs attached.
acme_dev: Curl we used:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary @payload.ndjson.gz
```
acme_dev: payload.ndjson.gz is gzip of a file that contains 3 lines, each a JSON string: e.g.
```
"first sentence"
"second sentence"
"third sentence"
```
samir: Quick suspicion: Content-Type is wrong for NDJSON. If you set application/json the server tries to parse the (gzipped) body as one JSON document. Combined with the gzip header it sometimes ends up treated as a single string input. Use Content-Type: application/x-ndjson when streaming newline-delimited inputs.
devon: Also watch for double-stringifying. Some client libs produce lines like `"[\"first\"]"` (a string that contains JSON), which becomes a nested array on our side -> shape mismatch. Common pattern: client does JSON.stringify on an already-stringified line.
olivia: Server log snippet (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-12T14:02:01Z] req_id=xyz received_content_encoding=gzip content_type=application/json lines=1 expected_lines=3 embeddings_returned=1
[2026-02-12T14:02:01Z] req_id=xyz parse_warning=ndjson_parse_failed fallback=single_input
```
samir: Repro locally for us: create a plain text file with three raw lines (not JSON-wrapped), gzip it, then send with headers:
```
Content-Type: application/x-ndjson
Content-Encoding: gzip
```
That yields 3 inputs and 3 embeddings. If you must send JSON (application/json) then send a top-level array: `[{"input":"a"},{"input":"b"}]` un-gzipped.
acme_dev: Ah — our pipeline gzips earlier and a wrapper code did JSON.stringify on the file contents before gzip. That explains double-encoding.
samir: Quick suggested fixes:
- For newline-delimited inputs: ensure each line is the raw text (or raw JSON object per line) and set Content-Type: application/x-ndjson. Do NOT JSON.stringify the whole file before gzipping.
- For single/batch JSON: send a valid JSON array (application/json), un-gzipped or with matching content-encoding.
- If client libs auto-wrap single items into arrays, verify they don't produce nested arrays. Flatten before sending: `const payload = items.map(x => (Array.isArray(x) ? x.flat() : x))`.
devon: Example minimal JS fix for NDJSON gzip:
```js
const zlib = require('zlib');
const lines = texts.map(t => t.replace(/\n/g,' ')).join('\n');
const gz = zlib.gzipSync(Buffer.from(lines));
// send gz as binary with headers: Content-Type: application/x-ndjson, Content-Encoding: gzip
```
olivia: I've asked Acme to try that. Also added a KB note to the support queue explaining the Content-Type vs NDJSON gotcha.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: added additional parse warning telemetry for mismatched content-type + content-encoding (low risk) to help catch these sooner.
acme_dev: Confirmed — switched to application/x-ndjson + removed extra stringify step. Now we get 3 embeddings, counts align, billing returned to expected. Thanks :tada:
samir: Nice. I'll follow up with a short doc blurb and add a unit test to our NDJSON gzip parsing path to avoid silent fallback to single-input.
devon: Marking as resolved from infra side. Closing thread after KB update.
